predecessors.name: Ashikaga shogunate
predecessors.text: the Ashikaga shogunate's national realm of 1459-1467, of which the shogunate keeps only the Kyoto remnant from 1468

successors.name: Tokugawa shogunate
successors.text: the lands of the Western Army and the rest of Japan, over which 'the Tokugawa clan gains nominal control of all Japan' after Sekigahara on 21 October 1600

ledger.x: 1467: the Ōnin War breaks out in Kyoto and 'initiated the Sengoku period'.
1468: outside Kyoto the shogunate no longer rules.
1477: the Ōnin War ends in Kyoto. Ōuchi Masahiro 'left the area on 17 December 1477'; 'By 1477, ten years after the fighting had begun, Kyoto was nothing more than a place for mobs to loot.'
1488: the Kaga Ikkō-ikki takes Kaga Province.
1552: the shape extends into southern Hokkaido (Oshima Peninsula, Hakodate side).
1573: Nobunaga ends the Ashikaga shogunate and takes Kyoto.
1573: the Sengoku period gives way to the Azuchi-Momoyama period under Nobunaga.
1600: the eastern half goes to the Tokugawa.
1600: Sekigahara hands the western half to the Tokugawa.
1600: the Sengoku-Azuchi-Momoyama state ends at Sekigahara.

wars.name: Ōnin War
wars.outcome: No victor: it ended in December 1477 with the Ashikaga bakufu reduced to a Kyoto power and the provinces in the hands of daimyo; 'The war initiated the Sengoku period'.

wars.name: Kaga Rebellion
wars.outcome: The Kaga ikki assumed control of the entire province and kept it for nearly 100 years.

wars.name: Ishiyama Hongan-ji War
wars.outcome: Oda took Ishiyama Hongan-ji 'in 1580 after an 11-year siege' (Ikkō-ikki page); the Kaga Province page says Shibata Katsuie conquered Kaga without a year.

wars.name: Shikoku campaign (Hideyoshi)
wars.outcome: 'The daimyo of the Shikoku Chōsokabe clan surrendered to Hideyoshi in July, 1585.'

wars.name: Kyushu campaign (Hideyoshi)
wars.outcome: 'Hideyoshi conquered Kyushu in the Kyushu Campaign (1586-1587) from the Shimazu clan.'

wars.name: Siege of Odawara
wars.outcome: 'In 1590, at the head of an army of 200,000, Hideyoshi defeated the Later Hōjō clan'; the Tōhoku clans swore allegiance and the Sengoku page says this 'finally achieved the unification of Japan'.

wars.name: Japanese invasions of Korea (Imjin War)
wars.outcome: Joseon and Ming victory; territorial change 'Status quo ante bellum'; the Japanese left in December 1598 after Hideyoshi's death and the defeat at Noryang.

wars.name: Siege of Ulsan
wars.outcome: 'Withdrawal of Korean and Ming forces': an 'unsuccessful Ming-Joseon attempt to capture Ulsan from the Japanese', 26 January to 19 February 1598.

wars.name: Battle of Sekigahara
wars.outcome: Eastern Army (Tokugawa) victory on 21 October 1600; 'Tokugawa clan gains nominal control of all Japan'.

certainty.note: A land of competing daimyo: no treaty or survey line is on the pages, and the one shape per year is Cliopatria's abstraction.
